chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned to his companions and said: 'Take up shields.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, is it from an enemy who has surrounded us?' He replied, 'No, but from the Fire. Say: Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu Akbar.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the four phrases recommended to protect oneself from the Hellfire?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) metaphorically instructs his companions to use the four *Tasbihat* (glorifications) as spiritual armor against the Hellfire, shifting the focus from physical warfare to inner purification. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on the protective power of dhikr, where specific verbal invocations serve as a divine shield for the believer's soul. The narration highlights the practical application of these phrases as a continuous defense mechanism against spiritual peril.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Sa’d ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from Tha’laba ibn Maymun, from Yunus ibn Ya’qub, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (as), who said: "

The Messenger of Allah (saw) turned to his companions and said: 'Take up shields.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, is it from an enemy who has surrounded us?' He replied, 'No, but from the fire (of Hell). Say: Subhanallah (Glory be to Allah), Alhamdulillah (Praise be to Allah), La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), and Allahu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest).'"
